claim: Gerber & Green (2000) effect sizes: personal canvassing raised turnout by 9.8 percentage points; direct mail raised turnout by 0.6 percentage points per mailing; telephone calls had no effect and may have slightly decreased turnout.
stance_target: relative cost-effectiveness ranking of field-contact channels used to justify prioritizing door-to-door in militant targeting strategy
scope_conditions: New Haven, Connecticut, USA, 1998 election; figures as summarized on an academia.edu preview page, not independently verified against original tables
quoted_support: Personal canvassing increases voter turnout by 9.8 percentage points, emphasizing its effectiveness over other methods... Direct mail raised turnout by 0.6 percentage points per mailing, suggesting limited effectiveness.
